title: Hubble Interacting Galaxy NGC 7674
caption: Galaxy NGC 7674 in the Hickson 96 group, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 7674, Mrk 533, HCG 96, Arp 182, VV 343a · constellation Pegasus
credit: NASA, ESA, the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration, and A. Evans (University of Virginia, Charlottesville/NRAO/Stony Brook University)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Just above the center of the frame, a spiral galaxy faces us almost head-on, with a bar of stars across its middle and long, narrow streamers reaching out to the left and below. This is NGC 7674, also called Markarian 533, the largest and brightest of the four galaxies in a compact group known as Hickson 96.

The streamers are tidal features. Gravitational pulls from neighboring galaxies in the group can explain the spiral's distorted shape, and the same encounters may be feeding its core. Its powerful active nucleus is of the kind called a type 2 Seyfert, and NASA suggests it is perhaps fueled by gas drawn toward the center as the companions tug on the galaxy.

NGC 7674 belongs to the family of luminous infrared galaxies, and it appears as number 182 in Arp's Atlas of Peculiar Galaxies. It lies in Pegasus, the Winged Horse, about 400 million light-years from Earth according to NASA.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took this image. NASA has not published which filters were used or how colors were assigned.
understand.eye: The 33-minute exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, which helps bring out faint structure such as the streamers.

explore: The image is one of a set of 59 merging-galaxy pictures released on 24 April 2008, the telescope's 18th launch anniversary. The galaxy is also cataloged as VV 343a, and its group as HCG 96.
alt: A face-on barred spiral galaxy just above center with long, narrow streamers extending to the left and below.
